subject: journalism
intro: Journalism leads to the roles that gather, check and publish the news — reporting, editing, photography and video storytelling across print, broadcast and digital platforms.

roles.title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
roles.what: Narrate or write news stories, reviews and commentary for print, broadcast or online media, collecting and analysing information through interviews, investigation and observation before publication.
roles.where: The Essential journalism unit is the core craft: finding and assessing stories, news writing, interviewing and features. Media law (defamation, contempt, court reporting) and the data journalism elective supply the verification and statistics scepticism the job demands.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Plan, coordinate, revise and edit written material, reviewing proposals and drafts for publication and shaping copy so it is accurate, readable and ready for the audience.
roles.where: Sub-editing and editorial decision-making is a topic of the Essential journalism unit, and the Editing skills for journalists elective covers house style, headlines, captions and layout — the daily toolkit of an editor.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Originate and prepare written material — scripts, stories, advertisements and other content — developing ideas from first draft to publishable copy for a range of outlets and clients.
roles.where: Feature writing and the sports journalism and business and finance journalism electives train exactly this origination and drafting; the public affairs elective adds the subject knowledge behind informed non-fiction writing.

roles.title: Photographers
roles.what: Photograph people, events and subjects, including photojournalism, using lighting to shape the image and editing software to produce the finished pictures that accompany and carry stories.
roles.where: The videojournalism elective's shooting and editing for online platforms and the e-portfolio unit's published work across platforms give the visual storytelling and picture-editing habits photojournalism runs on.

roles.title: Film and Video Editors
roles.what: Edit moving images on video or other media, organising shots into a final production and synchronising soundtracks, usually working to a producer's or director's brief.
roles.where: The videojournalism for digital platforms elective — shooting and editing video for online, mobile and social storytelling — plus the e-portfolio's cross-platform published work are the exact competencies editors use daily.
